text:
Jane M.: Hey eng-runtime — we need a quick, reproducible bench set for next week's webinar. Can you help with a prioritized list of payloads + traffic profiles we should run?
Sam G.: timeline? we have slides and live demo; ideally numbers by Tue EOD.
Priya K.: need p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimates. Also a short note on methodology for the deck.
Alex L.: tagging runtime-bot and Maya. We can do this. Two clarifying q's: (1) do you want quantized variants + FP16? (2) exact prompt families or sample corpus?
Maya S.: agree with Alex. Also need target sequence lengths and concurrency profile (single-request latency vs burst).
runtime-bot: queued job template: https://internal.redwood/runbook/jobs/bench-template (private)
Jane M.: prioritize what looks best on a slide and in a 10-min demo. We want: short chat reply (<=64 tokens), long completion (>=1024 tokens), embedding latency for 512-dim, and a 200-token summarization. Single-request and 100rps burst profiles. Include quantized where feasible.
Alex L.: got it. Suggestion: run each payload across: {fp16, int8-quant}, with seq lengths [64, 256, 1024], and two concurrency profiles: 1 qps and 100 rps burst (100 concurrent). Also capture cold-start (empty KV cache) and warm (with cached prefixes).
Priya K.: that aligns w/ product messaging. Can you include a tiny reproducibility note we can paste: random_seed, model_version, machine_type?
Maya S.: yes — we'll record: seed, model sha, env (docker image), runtime flags. Example run command we'll share:```bash
RUN_SEED=42 ./run_bench --model redwood-large-v2 --precision fp16 --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 100 --cache-mode warm
```
Alex L.: also adding minimal config snippet for quantization pipeline:```json
{
  "quantize": true,
  "backend": "int8",
  "calib_samples": 500
}
```
Sam G.: awesome. Any blockers for Tue EOD? If you need access or priority we can escalate.
Maya S.: main blocker is GPU queue time. If marketing can accept preliminary numbers from a single zone (us-west1) by Tue, final cross-region sweep by Thu is doable.
Jane M.: ok single-zone prelim is fine. We'll footnote "prelim — us-west1". Can you also export CSV with columns: payload_id, model, variant, seq_len, concurrency, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tps, cpu_pct, gpu_mem_gb, cost_per_1k_tokens?
Alex L.: yes we will produce that CSV and a short methodology blurb. We'll also include raw outputs and a small set of example inputs/outputs for the appendix.
Priya K.: we'll need a 1-paragraph blurb summarizing what changed between quantized and fp16 on latency and quality tradeoffs. Can you capture a couple of qualitative notes?
Maya S.: we can run an automated quality compare on a 50-sample eval set and give delta rates (exact-match/fluency flags). Not a full eval but should surface big regressions.
Jane M.: perfect. Who's owning the preliminary run?
Alex L.: Maya and I will own bench runs. Estimated prelim deliverable Tue 18:00 PT.
Sam G.: I'll add a task to the webinar checklist and link the CSV when ready.
Priya K.: thanks — can you ping this thread when the CSV/slide blurb is uploaded?
runtime-bot: job scheduled: bench/prelim/1852468012, owner: maya.s, eta: 2025-10-14T18:00:00-07:00
Maya S.: ping back when uploads are live. We'll include a link to a short dashboard + raw artifacts.
Jane M.: thanks everyone. If queue time shifts, we'll accept a small N=3 warm-run median instead of full sweep. :thumbsup:
Alex L.: noted. Will follow up if we hit >2h queue.
Priya K.: appreciate it.
Sam G.: cheers :rocket:
